ios.desc:
liiists is a fast, beautiful list app.

Every list you make is a plain markdown file on your device. No proprietary database. No server you can't see. No login. You can read your lists with any text editor, sync them through iCloud Drive, edit them from your laptop, or pipe them through your own scripts.

If you ever leave liiists, your data leaves with you, exactly as you wrote it.

FEATURES

• Markdown-native. Every list is a .md file you own.
• Two list types: regular lists and checklists.
• iCloud Drive sync. Your lists everywhere, no account required.
• Suggest More AI. Tap once to get a handful of new items that fit your list, generated on-device with Apple Intelligence (iOS 26+, Apple Intelligence-capable devices).
• Nothing-inspired design. Dot-matrix typography, monochrome, zero clutter.
• Widgets, Siri Shortcuts, Share Sheet, search.
• Publish a list as a shareable web page.
• "Add a bunch" multi-line paste.

PRIVACY

liiists stores your lists on your device and, if you have iCloud sync turned on, in your private iCloud Drive container. We don't run servers of our own. Suggest More uses Apple's on-device foundation model, so the prompt and the suggestions it returns never leave your phone.

From Enigma Studio Inc., Toronto.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Liiists, a Markdown-first, iOS and CLI list app

quotes.text:
This is the first app I've made that got all the way to "live." I started to learn this whole vibe-coding thing, and decided to publish/share because I quite like using it myself!

Github: https://github.com/djt53/liiists
iOS app: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/liiists/id6761671906

It's a pretty simple list app, with three types of lists:

- Lists (self explanatory)
- Checklists (also pretty straightforward)
- Logs (like lists, but with an adjustable time stamp)

It has a few basic things that I added to address reasons I've never stuck with other list-app options (despite really liking making lists):

- Markdown-first: nothing fancy
- Local friendly: if you have iCloud enabled, all your lists are just .md files on your computer as well as in the app
- CLI / iOS either or: Plays nicely with a terminal / claude code (brew install djt53/liiists/liiists); you can use the app without the CLI, and the CLI without the app

And a few more playful things, just for fun:

- Discover other users' lists (and publish your own if you'd like)
- Suggest new elements in a list (using Apple on device AI)
